Marine Affairs URI’s Department of Marine Affairs offers the following degrees: B.A., B.S., M.A., M.M.A. (Master of Marine Affairs), and Ph.D.
The B.A. and B.S. in marine affairs focus on coastal and ocean areas and examine environmental resources, human uses, and governance from a variety of perspectives.

Topics include conservation, ocean policy and law, climate adaptation and resilience, tourism and recreation, environmental justice, ocean energy resources, coastal and island communities, ports and shipping, fisheries and marine ecosystems, spatial planning and management.
A marine affairs major establishes a background for careers in the public or private sectors in a wide variety of marine-related fields.
Typical areas of employment include positions in government concerned with coastal zone, environmental, or fishery management, and marine transportation.
In the private sectors, students have secured positions in environmental consulting firms, marine insurance, public interest nongovernmental organizations, marinas, ports, and companies involved in shipping.

This program builds on the long-standing reputation of the University of Rhode Island as a national and international leader in the field of geospatial technology, particularly GIS.
The Environmental Data Center, a research lab in the Department of Natural Resource Science is considered the state's center of technical expertise in the field.
The power and timeliness of geospatial technologies is more apparent than ever.
Geospatial tools have driven the delivery of Covid-19 data to the public and decision makers.
Spatial patterns of the magnitude of outbreaks, dashboards (e.g., WHO) summarizing local conditions and visualizations of trends are all the result of geospatial technologies.
GIS Story Maps examining the history of transmission have appeared in the NY Times and other venues.
Geospatial technologies are used extensively across many sectors of the economy and are a critical support tool for resource management, planning, disaster management and mitigation, and community health, among others.

Increasingly, an expectation exists among employers that graduates will have working knowledge and understanding of geospatial technologies as they seek positions in the private and public sectors.
GIS is considered a high growth field, according to U.S Department of Labor and Statistics.
O- Net Online has compiled the data and found that employment in the GIS field is expected to grow 7 - 10 % faster than average, with 35,700 job openings in the U.S expected between 2018 - 2028.
Internationally, GIS analytical skills are highly sought after, and the certificate should be very attractive to students in developing countries.
Geospatial technology is rapidly evolving, and professionals are interested in expanding or acquiring the necessary skills to employ state-of-the-art techniques for collecting, analyzing, interpreting, managing, and presenting location-based data.

An Online Graduate Certificate in GIS and Geospatial Technologies will allow learning opportunities for a wider audience and provide flexibility to accommodate and meet the needs of domestic and international students, working professionals, active and reserve service members and those seeking to acquire a powerful and practical skill set for employment.

The courses will focus on tools and technologies available within the Esri ArcGIS Desktop & Online platforms, considered to be the cross-industry standard for everything geospatial.

Course format and learning activities will emphasize critical spatial analysis techniques, data management and creative workflows for data analysis, capture and presentation, critical skills for modern day geospatial analysts and managers at all levels.

State the program objectives.
The focus of the Online Graduate Certificate in GIS and Geospatial Technologies is two-fold: 1) to prepare students for opportunities in the expanding field of geospatial technologies and offer a workforce pipeline of graduates to meet the demand for geospatial analysts in the public and private sectors nationally and abroad; and 2) to facilitate enrollment and completion of the URI professional Master of Environmental Science and Management (MESM).

The lab is considered the state's center of technical expertise in the field and has extensive contacts in the private and public sectors that will aid in marketing the program.
In addition, several hundred working professionals have taken short courses offered by URI's Geospatial Training Program, taught by the extension educators associated with this proposed certificate, many of these participants express interest in further training.
Given the increasing demand for trained personnel in this field, academic institutions have responded by offering online graduate certificate programs for focused training in geospatial technology.

The University of Connecticut and University of Maine offer online GIS certificates but, market research shows that there is still unmet student demand for these types of programs (URI's Market Opportunity Scan; Hanover Research pg. 6) In addition, the URI program differs from existing regional options in two important ways.

The courses for this program will be designed and taught by the experienced geospatial technology practitioners of the EDC and the Geospatial Training Program.
The course content reflects workflows and strategies used in real-world application of GIS and geospatial technologies: data acquisition, data manipulation, analysis, visualization, and integration with other data sources.

Second, the URI program is unique in that it was intentionally designed to allow graduates to apply to the Masters of Environmental Science and Management (MESM) program and, if accepted, earn a master's degree after just 2 additional semesters on campus since all 12 of their certificate credits would count toward MESM course requirements.
